title: Zoids Franchise Announces New Zoids: Chaotic Century Manga
content:
The official X (formerly Twitter ) account for Takara Tomy 's Zoids franchise announced on Friday that a new manga tentatively titled Zoids: Chaotic Century Kanketsu-hen (Zoids: Chaotic Century Final Chapter) is currently in the works. More details about the manga will be announced at a later date.

The Zoids: Chaotic Century manga by Michiro Ueyama ran in Shogakukan 's Monthly Coro Coro Comics magazine from 1999 to 2001.

The first Zoids: Chaotic Century anime premiered in 1999.

The anime franchise most recently celebrated its 25th anniversary in July 2024 with various projects such as a pop-up shop tour, cast talk shows, collaborative menus, and anime releases on streaming services.

Takara Tomy announced the Zoids Wild project in 2018 as the latest installment in its Zoids franchise . The project includes anime, manga, model kits, and two Nintendo Switch games.

Naoto Tsushima launched a manga crossover between the Zoids and Patlabor franchises titled Zoids x Patlabor -Code Name B.U.D.D.Y.- on IMAGICA Infos ' Hero Comics website in August 2025.
author: ANN

title: Blue Box Season 2 Creditless Opening and Ending Videos Revealed
content:
Blue Box Season 2 revealed the creditless opening and ending video sequences following its premiere on October 4, 2026. Singer aiko is performing “Anata no Hana no Iro” for the opening theme song, while the band elsewhere kikou sings “blue in” for the ending theme song.

You can watch the opening below.

Also check out the ending:

Studio Electric Circus is animating the second season, replacing Telecom Animation Film. Daisuke Sako is the new director, taking over from Yuichiro Yano. The returning staff includes Yuko Kakihara as the one handling the series composition, Miho Tanino as character designer, and features music by Takashi Omama.

• Shoya Chiba as Taiki Inomata

• Reina Ueda as Chinatsu Kano

• Akari Kito as Hina Chono

• Chiaki Kobayashi as Kyo Kasahara

• Kana Ichinose as Ayame Moriya

• Yuma Uchida as Kengo Hanyu

Koji Miura writes and draws the manga for Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine. The manga began serialization in April 2021 and has 24 published volumes as of February 2026. MANGA Plus describes Miura’s Blue Box manga: Taiki Inomata is on the boys’ badminton team at sports powerhouse Eimei Junior and Senior High. He’s in love with basketball player Chinatsu Kano, the older girl he trains alongside every morning in the gym. One Spring day, their relationship takes a sharp turn … And thus begins this brand-new series of love, sports and youth! Source: TMS Entertainment Official YouTube © Kouji Miura /SHUEISHA/ Blue Box Film Partners

title: Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend Film Announces Text Story Bonus Item for Moviegoers
content:
The staff for Seishun Buta Yarō wa Dear Friend no Yume o Minai ( Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend ) film, the latest anime of Hajime Kamoshida 's Rascal Does Not Dream ( Seishun Buta Yarō or Aobuta ) novel series, revealed on Saturday fans who see the film in the first week of release will receive a bonus new text story written by Kamoshida titled Seishun Buta Yarō wa Tea Garden no Yume o Miru (Rascal Does Dream of a Tea Garden).

The short story follows Sakuta, Mai and Shoko after a shopping trip. Keeji Mizoguchi illustrates the short story.

The film will open in theaters in Japan on October 16. The new film is teased as taking the story towards its finale. (The film shares the same name as the 15th and final novel volume.)

The staff will hold an advance screening of the film with the cast on October 4 at the Shinjuku Wald 9 theater in Tokyo.

The film's returning cast includes:

• Kaito Ishikawa as Sakuta Azusagawa

• Asami Seto as Mai Sakurajima

• Sora Amamiya as Uzuki Hirokawa

• Aya Yamane as Ikumi Akagi

• Konomi Kohara as Sara Himeji

• Manaka Iwami as Miori Mitō

• Reina Ueda as Nene Iwamizawa

• Nao Tōyama as Tomoe Koga

• Atsumi Tanezaki as Rio Futaba

• Maaya Uchida as Nodoka Toyohama

• Yurika Kubo as Kaede Azusagawa

• Inori Minase as Shōko Makinohara

Sōichi Masui returns to direct the film at CloverWorks . Masahiro Yokotani is also back to oversee and write the script, and Satomi Tamura is again designing the characters. The band fox capture plan also returns to compose the music. Aniplex is once again distributing the film.

Tōko Kirishima performs the song "Turn the World Upside Down" in the film and the theme song "Suihei-sen wa Boku no Furukizu finale" (The Horizon Is My Old Wound: Finale).

Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai ( Seishun Buta Yarō wa Bunny Girl-senpai no Yume wo Minai ), the first television anime based on the light novel series, premiered in Japan in October 2018 and aired for 13 episodes. The anime adapts the story up to the fifth novel volume. Aniplex of America streamed the series on Crunchyroll , Funimation , and other services.

Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl ( Seishun Buta Yarō wa Yume-Miru Shōjo no Yume wo Minai ), the anime film that adapts the the sixth and seventh light novel volumes in the franchise, opened in Japan in June 2019. Aniplex of America and Funimation Films screened the anime in the United States. Crunchyroll began streaming the film in June 2025 with both English subtitles and dub .

The film Rascal Does Not Dream of a Sister Venturing Out opened in Japan in June 2023. The film sold 118,108 tickets in its first three days and earned 175,648,924 yen (about US$1.28 million) to rank #4 in its opening weekend. The Rascal Does Not Dream of a Knapsack Kid film opened in Japan in December 2023, and ranked at #4 in its opening weekend. The film sold 119,000 tickets and earned 164,594,554 yen (about US$1.11 million) in its first three days.

Rascal Does Not Dream of Santa Claus ( Seishun Buta Yarō wa Santa Claus no Yume wo Minai ), the television anime adapting the light novel series' "University Student Arc," debuted in July 2025. Crunchyroll streamed the anime as it aired, and is also streaming an English dub .

The original novel series has over 3 million copies in circulation. The Yen On imprint of Yen Press publishes the novel series, and Yen Press publishes Tsugumi Nanamiya 's manga adaptation. Yen On published the Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dear Friend novel volume on January 6.

title: Suikoden Anime to Stream on YouTube with English Subtitles
content:
The official English YouTube channel for Suikoden: The Anime , the adaptation of Konami 's Suikoden II game's story, announced in a video on Saturday the series will stream with English subtitles on YouTube for free beginning October 6 with new episodes on Tuesdays.

The stream will be available in North America, Latin America, the Caribbean, Ireland, parts of Africa and the Middle East, and in New Zealand and Australia. The staff have listed the full region availability on the anime's X/Twitter account in English.

Ani-One Asia has also licensed the anime.

Konami describes Suikoden II :

Our story's hero and his friend Jowy are members of the Unicorn Youth Brigade, which participated in a drawn-out border dispute between the Highland Kingdom and the City-States of Jowstown. A few months earlier, a truth agreement was signed between the two forces, both of which were happy to see an end to the fighting. However, hidden under the momentary peace the fires of a new war continued to smolder…

Previously announced cast members include:

• Toshiki Kumagai as Riliu

• Shimba Tsuchiya as Jowy

• Ayumi Hinohara as Nanami

• Katsuyuki Konishi as Viktor

• Yūichi Nakamura as Flik

• Taku Yashiro as Luca Blight

• Chika Anzai as Jillia Blight

• Akihiro Mine as Rowd

• Tsukino Chikasada as Pilika

• Ayumu Murase as Luc

• Takeo Ōtsuka as Shu

• Yoshino Aoyama as Apple

• Masato Niwa as Mukumuku

• Jun Kasama as Culgan

• Yoshitsugu Matsuoka as Seed

• Megumi Han as Leknaat

• Shōta Hayama as Gengen

• Ryūnosuke Watanuki as Rikimaru

• Saya Hitomi as Rina

• Mizutama Umino as Eilie

• Yūsuke Sasaki as Bolgan

• Jin Yamanoi as Agares Blight

• Miyuki Sawashiro as Anabelle

• Kōdai Sakai as Jess

Yūzō Satō (credited as just YUZO on the anime's English website) is directing the anime at KONAMI animation , the game studio's anime studio. NBCUniversal Entertainment Japan anime and music production department member Ryō Hino serves as the producer and production manager.

Michihiro Tsuchiya ( PriPara , ClassicaLoid ) is overseeing the series scripts. Fumi Ishikawa from Konami Digital Entertainment is credited as the game character designer, Arata Suzuki from Konami Digital Entertainment is credited for the original drafts of the anime character designs, and Ryō Yamauchi ( My Master Has No Tail ; Please Put Them On, Takamine-san! ) is the anime character designer. Yoshikazu Iwanami ( Psycho-Pass , Ghost in the Shell Arise ) is the sound director, and Kōji Nakamura ( EUREKA SEVEN AO , Ping Pong live-action film) is composing the music.

Suikoden I&II HD Remaster Gate Rune and Dunan Unification Wars , the HD remastered release of Konami 's classic role-playing games Suikoden and Suikoden II , launched for Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, and PC via Steam in March 2025.

Konami released the original game for the PlayStation in 1995, followed by the sequel game in 1998. The series has five main installments and five spinoff games.

Konami is also developing the new mobile and PC game Gensō Suikoden : Star Leap , which launched for iOS and Android on August 7 in Japan. The game is also slated for PC via Steam . The developers assured players on August 7 the will have a release in English, French, German, Korean, and Chinese (Simplified and Traditional).

title: Amazon Prime Video Streams The Seven Knights of the Marronnier Kingdom Anime With Same-Day English Dub
content:
Amazon Prime Video added the television anime of Nao Iwamoto 's Marronnier Ōkoku no Shichinin no Kishi ( The Seven Knights of the Marronnier Kingdom ) manga on Saturday, with English subtitles along with an English dub .

The English dub cast and staff include:

Dub cast:

• Kevin Andrew Rivera as Insomniac

• Daniel Sean Smith as Chilly

• Chelsea Krause as Baribara

• Mariah Tzoumbas as Bruno / Brunhild

• Paul Castro Jr. as Fraternity

• Ryan Bartley as Hungry

• John Patneaude as Swordsman

• Skyler Brigmann as Feverish

• Corey Holland as Beast-Tamer

• Additional voices: Aeric Azana, Ted Evans, Ryan Bartley, Corey Holland, Tara Sands, Keith Silverstein, Kennedy Hibbert

Dub staff:

• Dubbing Studio: Deluxe Los Angeles

• Dubbing Director: Brett Calo

• Script Adapter: Djamel Bennecib

• Casting Director: Brett Calo

• Recording Engineer: Dennis D'Angelo

• Dialogue Editor: Walter Ledesma

• Re-Recording Mixer: Walter Ledesma

• Dubbing Producer: Boris Isaac

• Dubbing Coordinator: Kamen Tagalicod

The anime debuted on October 3 on the NHK Educational channel at 6:25 p.m. JST (5:25 a.m. EDT).

The anime stars:

• Kengo Takanashi as Nemukunai (Insomniac)

• Makoto Tanikawa as Hakuai (Fraternity)

• Haruki Ishiya as Atsugariya (Feverish)

• Satoshi Inomata as Samugariya (Chilly)

• Kiyoto Mizuno as Kemono Tsukai (Beast-Tamer)

• Taishi Murata as Tsurugi Jiman (Swordsman)

• Reiji Kawashima as Harapeko (Hungry)

• Akeno Watanabe as Baribara

• Show Hayami as Narrator

Kiyoko Sayama ( Skip Beat! , Vampire Knight , To Your Eternity seasons 2-3) is directing the anime at J.C. Staff . Shinzō Fujita ( To Your Eternity seasons 1-3, The World Is Still Beautiful ) is both writing and overseeing the series scripts. Yuriko Maeda (chief animation director for Requiem of the Rose King , One Punch Man TV 2 ) is designing the characters, Yoshiaki Fujisawa ( Apocalypse Hotel , Land of the Lustrous , Love Live! School idol project ) is composing the music, and Jin Aketagawa ( Dr. Stone , Fire Force ) is the sound director.

Viz Media licensed the manga on Thursday and uploaded the first two chapters digitally on the same day.

The fantasy romance manga centers on seven brothers who are knights of the Marronnier Kingdom. The kingdom lies in the center of a group of eight kingdoms, and each brother is dispatched to a different kingdom as ambassadors, to go on an adventure to find their fated partner.

The manga launched in Shogakukan 's Flowers magazine in 2016. Shogakukan shipped the 11th volume on June 10. The manga topped the list of manga for female readers in the 2018 edition of Takarajimasha 's Kono Manga ga Sugoi! (This Manga Is Amazing!) guidebook.
author: ANN

title: Crunchyroll Streams New Sgt. Frog TV Anime
content:
Crunchyroll added Keroro Gunsō ☆ , an all-new Sgt. Frog television anime , to the streaming service with English subtitles on Friday. The company is streaming the anime under the title KERORO☆ , and is streaming the series worldwide except in Asia.

The anime features an all-new cast for the franchise. The previous Shin Gekijōban ☆ Keroro Gunsō Fukkatsu Shite Sokkō Chikyū Metsubō no Kiki de Arimasu! film that opened in June featured a returning cast from previous installments in the anime.

The cast includes:

• Kōsuke Echigoya as Sergeant Major Kululu

• Rika Nagae as Private Second Class Tamama

• Makoto Koichi as Sergeant Keroro

• Toshiki Masuda as Corporal Giroro

• Satoshi Inomata as Lance Corporal Dororo

• Yuki Sakakihara as Fuyuki Hinata

• Minori Fujidera as Natsumi Hinata

• Sumire Morohoshi as Momoka Nishizawa

• Hiiro Ishibashi as Mutsumi Hōjō

• Koko Fukushima as Koyuki Azumaya

Nobuhiro Kondō ( Shōnen Ashibe GO! GO! Goma-chan four seasons, Yu-Gi-Oh! Sevens , Cardfight!! Vanguard GZ ) is the chief director of the anime, and Akihiko Sano ( Farmagia , animation director for Medaka Box ) is directing the series at BN Pictures with production cooperation by Bridge and AISLE . Toshimitsu Takeuchi ( Shōnen Ashibe GO! GO! Goma-chan four seasons, Yu-Gi-Oh! Sevens , Fairy Musketeers ) is overseeing the series scripts, and Hatsue Nakayama ( Cardfight!! Vanguard GZ ) is designing the characters. Kan Sawada ( Shin Gekijōban ☆ Keroro Gunsō Fukkatsu Shite Sokkō Chikyū Metsubō no Kiki de Arimasu! , Yowamushi Pedal anime franchise) is composing the music.

Additional staff members include:

• Color Design: Keiichi Funada

• Art Director: Kenichi Tajiri, Shintarō Inoue

• Director of Photography: Teruyuki Kawase

• Editing: Daisuke Imai

• Sound Director: Haru Yamada

Shin Gekijōban ☆ Keroro Gunsō Fukkatsu Shite Sokkō Chikyū Metsubō no Kiki de Arimasu! (New Sgt. Frog the Movie: The Earth Is in Mortal Peril as Soon as We Come Back!), the new 20th anniversary anime film project for the franchise, opened in Japan on June 26. The film ranked at #4 in its opening weekend, earning 150,809,200 yen (about US$927,900) in its first three days.

Crunchyroll added the earlier television anime to its catalog beginning in 2021, and it describes the anime:

Keroro is Sergeant Frog - the leader of a platoon of warriors sent to conquer planet Earth. But when the amphibious invaders discovered how much humans enjoy dissecting their comrades, the troops were scattered, the mission was aborted, and Keroro was abandoned. Now, this once proud soldier spends more time wielding a vacuum than he does the weapons of war. It's a far cry from the glory of battle, but hey, at least he's got his own room. And though the invasion may have slowed to a hop, Sergeant Frog still occasionally yearns to overcome his karaoke addiction and reassemble his troops.

Sunrise 's earlier anime series based on Mine Yoshizaki 's Sgt. Frog ( Keroro Gunsō ) manga ran from 2004 to 2011, and it spawned five feature films. Funimation released two "seasons" of the anime on DVD, after ADV Films had licensed but not released the anime.

Discotek licensed the anime, and its release of Sgt. Frog includes all 358 episodes in successive SD Blu-ray Disc volume releases by season, beginning in 2021. Discotek released seasons 5-7 in 2024.

American manga publisher Tokyopop released 20 volumes of the original manga in North America before shutting its doors in 2011.

title: 5 Major Reveals We Could See at Jump Festa 2027
content:
Shueisha is gearing up for one of its biggest events of the year, Jump Festa, which is a prominent event for fans to learn about various updates for Shonen Jump franchises, covering both anime and manga. The event is all set for the December 19-20 weekend, and the lineup for the event has also been unveiled. As it is every year, the event is going to be filled with three different stages.

While Jump Station and Jump Studio are two of the prominent stages, the Super Stage undoubtedly steals the show. title: The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 Is Back With the Elements That Prove It’s Still a Masterpiece
content:
The Fall 2026 season has arrived, and with its first weekend, it has also brought back everyone’s favorite drama anime, The Apothecary Diaries , with its third season on Crunchyroll. The second season of the series was one of its most amazing and intense installments, which led fans to question where the series would head next. Now, with the release of the first episode, it has confirmed exactly where it is moving, as the premiere didn’t waste any time setting up the elements of what is going to unfold this season. Starting off a little differently and slowly, the series places its two prominent characters, Jinshi and Maomao, in the perfect positions.

With her return to the Pleasure District, the first episode has already hinted that, after her ventures at the Imperial Palace, Maomao is now back in the streets, something that fans majorly love her for. Maomao’s curious nature is depicted through the slowness of the episode, which hints at what is going to be the next major threat of this season as well. Meanwhile, Jinshi continues his imperial political business, positioning him in the upcoming threat as well. By embracing the slowness and allowing viewers to invest and participate rather than explaining every element , this episode highlights why the series is a masterpiece.

The Apothecary Diaries Season 3 Begins by Perfectly Indulging the Viewers

One of the strengths of The Apothecary Diaries , and why it is so engaging for fans, is how the series depicts things in a way that involves the viewers as well. It does this by not explaining the elements right away, but as the characters unravel the mysteries, fans learn alongside them, giving them the sense of achievement that comes with discovering what is going on. This is exactly what is depicted in the premiere, which some might call boring due to its slow pacing, but it is in these quiet moments where the episode truly shines. In particular, it is Maomao’s moments in the first episode where this notion is depicted.

As Maomao is presented with locusts, she immediately begins to analyze the situation, connecting the dots rather than simply explaining it. The series does this profoundly, making it feel like the fans are actually discovering the mystery themselves. In the same episode, the series also presents other hints at how the locust plague is going to be a major element of this season, with a particularly interesting woman arriving to “help” a man who is already devastated by the locusts’ actions by giving him a sort of substance with which he would never feel hungry. With this, the season is clearly aiming toward a narrative where a famine crisis is going to be presented.

Somehow, even Jinshi is subtly hinted to be involved in the matter, which makes Maomao and Jinshi’s reunion in this season an even more epic journey. These elements already prove that The Apothecary Diaries has not just returned with a new season , but with the subtle, engaging elements that make it a masterpiece. Alongside its animation quality and sound design, it is already proving to be an epic return this fall, even among the great anime that are poised to return soon.

title: 20 Years Later, Shonen Jump Fans Are Still Waiting for This Anime to Return
content:
There’s no denying that when it comes to Shonen series, supernatural fantasies will always grab all the spotlight. One of the most standout original series of Weekly Shonen Jump is D.Gray-man , written and illustrated by Katsura Hoshino. The manga began serialization in 2004, but it wasn’t long after the debut that it started facing several hiatuses due to Hoshino’s health issues . In April 2018, the series moved to the quarterly magazine Jump SQ. Rise, leading to a far slower trickle for new chapters. Furthermore, although the manga is still ongoing, the latest chapters are only available in Japan.

Official platforms such as Viz Media and Shonen Jump only have 245 chapters available. On the bright side, the newer chapters are available in the latest Volume 29, which was only released recently . It’s the first manga volume released in three years, which is all the more reason why fans are hyped for the new release. The manga is commemorating its 20th anniversary since it debuted on October 3rd, 2026. Even 20 years and several hiatuses later, the series still maintains a wide global fan base, which is all the more reason why the anime needs to return as soon as possible.

D.Gray-man Returned With a Disappointing Sequel 10 Years Ago

While the anime originally debuted in 2008, it was an ongoing show that released weekly episodes. It didn’t take long before the anime caught up with the manga until there was no new content for the animation studio to adapt. The anime wrapped up after 103 episodes, leaving its future uncertain. This is all the more reason why its comeback with D.Gray-man Hallow in 2016 was supposed to be a big deal. Fans were enthusiastic to watch the sequel to their beloved show, but it wasn’t what they expected at all. The sequel should have received more hype since it was expected to be more visually polished.

Unfortunately, not only was the animation underwhelming, but the sequel even suffered from rushed pacing and several changes from the manga. Even so, despite the long wait, the sequel was a massive flop, and even the home video release was cancelled by Aniplex later on. The anime hasn’t confirmed any sequel for over a decade, even though there are enough chapters since the manga returned from hiatus. The anime has covered around 200 chapters, and it ended at a crucial phase right before around the time the story was getting even more intense.

D.Gray-man Needs a Reboot More Than a Sequel

There’s no denying that at this point, the anime would do better as a reboot since the earlier chapters weren’t always adapted perfectly either. Not to mention that since Hallow was a massive flop, the chances of a sequel being released are next to none. The anime fails to capture the gritty details and the true essence of the story that actually made it special. Not only that, but the 2000s animation and the long-running format aren’t that attractive to newer viewers either, which is why it’s becoming increasingly difficult for the series to rise in popularity. With the anime industry growing rapidly, fans have all kinds of new anime as options that have flashy animation on top of having an exceptional story.

While Hallow was definitely one of the worst adaptations , the original anime wasn’t exceptional either. Since it followed a weekly schedule, it suffered from slow pacing and even fillers. Even so, the biggest reason why the anime needs a reboot is just so it can perfectly capture the tone of the story. The manga is a lot darker than the anime portrayed it to be, which only got more intense as the story continued. Hoshino’s art style continued to evolve, further highlighting the brutality of the world Allen was forced to live in.

The mangaka’s art is deeply inspired by Gothic architecture, religious iconography, and classical European influences, which didn’t hit the same in the anime since it failed to properly capture these elements due to production constraints. Even though it might be a risky gamble, there’s no denying that fans would be more interested in the reboot if another studio decides to pick it up. The manga has over 27 million copies in circulation, which is a huge milestone for any series. It’s even more impressive considering that these sales are recorded after several hiatuses.

Head down to the comments to tell us if you are excited for the anime to return, or should it get a brand new adaptation instead? Or you could tell us your favorite D.Gray-man moment.

title: Kagurabachi Expands New Anime Cast With Special Trailer – Watch
content:
Kagurabachi is undoubtedly one of the huge Shonen Jump anime debuts fans are keeping an eye out for next year , and now the case of the series is getting even bigger with a cool new teaser trailer showing it off. Takeru Hokazono’s Kagurabachi has been pretty much begging to get its own anime adaptation ever since it made its original debut a few years ago, and thankfully the wait for that debut will soon be over. But each new look at the series is making the wait for it seem tougher.

Kagurabachi has been steadily revealing information over the course of the past few months as it has been in the midst of a world tour for its first episode’s early premiere . But there are still many things being kept under wraps like the majority of the characters we’ll see in action. Though one new face has been revealed as Yuichi Nakamura (Satoru Gojo in Jujutsu Kaisen , Loki in One Piece ) is joining the cast as Soshiro Azami. Check out the special trailer for the character below.

Kagurabachi Anime Recruits Yuichi Nakamura as Soshiro Azami

As detailed by CyberAgent in a new press release, Yuichi Nakamura has officially joined the cast of Kagurabachi as Soshiro Azami. The character is described as as a sorcerer affiliated with the Kamunabi (and teased to be one of the “most formidable members”), and is one of the few who know of Chihiro’s existence. Nakamura even teases bit of Azami’s charm as a character with, “I think he’s a character whose appeal will become increasingly apparent as the story progresses .”

Nakamura joins an already stacked cast for Kagurabachi that currently includes the likes of Taihi Kimura as Chihiro Rokuhira, Tomokazu Seki as Kunishige Rokuhira, Katsuyuki Konishi as Togo Shiba, Miyari Nemoto as Char Kyonagi, and Miku Ito as Hinao . It’s also been previously revealed that the new anime will be directed by Tetsuya Takeuchi for Cypic with Keigo Sasaki providing the character designs. But there’s still much that fans don’t know about the new anime’s production thus far. That will hopefully change soon enough.

When Does Kagurabachi Actually Come Out?

Kagurabachi will be making its debut on screens sometime next April as part of the Spring 2027 anime schedule. While there is no concrete release date for the new anime as of this time, it has been revealed that it will be streaming with Crunchyroll when it arrives . There are still many details fans are hoping to get revealed in the coming months too such as the production staff that’s bringing all of it to life. There is an opportunity for some big updates very soon, however.

Kagurabachi has been announced as one of the many titles that Shueisha will be showcasing as part of the Jump Festa 2027 event later this year . Taking place over the December 19-20 weekend in Japan, this is going to be where we likely get the biggest update for the new anime’s progress as we head into 2027. There likely will be other opportunities to showcase more heading into December, but we’ll have to see how it shakes out.

How are you liking how Kagurabachi’ s anime is coming together so far? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!
